nodes.title: feat: report unsafe labeled `continue` in `no-unsafe-finally` rule

data.title: Bug: `no-unsafe-finally` misses labeled `continue` targeting a loop outside `finally`
data.titleHTML: Bug: no-unsafe-finally misses labeled continue targeting a loop outside finally
data.bodyHTML:
Environment

Node version: v22.16.0
npm version: v11.17.0
Local ESLint version: v10.9.1
Global ESLint version: None
Operating System: macOS 26.5 (Apple Silicon, arm64)

What parser are you using?

Default (Espree)

What did you do?

Configuration 
export default [
    {
        rules: {
            "no-unsafe-finally": "error",
        },
    },
];
function foo() {
  outer: for (let i = 0; i < 1; i++) {
    try {
      return 1;
    } finally {
      for (let j = 0; j < 1; j++) {
        continue outer; // Not reported
      }
    }
  }

  return 2;
}

foo(); // 2

What did you expect to happen?

The labeled continue statement should be reported as unsafe.

What actually happened?

No error was reported.

Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

Playground

Participation

  • I am willing to submit a pull request for this issue.

AI acknowledgment

  • I did not use AI to generate this issue report.
  • (If the above is not checked) I have reviewed the AI-generated content before submitting.

Additional comments

The no-unsafe-finally rule disallows continue statements that can override a return or throw in try/catch. However, using continue inside finally as in the example cancels the pending return, so it should be reported.

Although this could be the code author’s intention, I think it would be good for no-unsafe-finally to report this as unsafe.

That's because the documentation also explains that

control flow statements inside try and catch are overwritten, which is considered as unexpected behavior.

And, I found that an invalid test case for the same structure was requested in #6000 (comment) 10 years ago.

I thought it would be better to ask in an issue first rather than submit a PR. I’d appreciate your thoughts on this. Thank you!

Disclosure: I'm a participant of open source contribution program OSSCA
